user.title: Connect to UniFi Play
user.description: Choose how to find your UniFi Play devices. Direct connection talks to the speakers themselves and works on any network — including consoles that have no Apollo application (UCG-Fiber, Cloud Key, and others).

console.title: Connect via UniFi OS Console
console.description: Enter your UDM Pro (or UniFi OS Console) IP address or hostname (without https://) and an API key.

direct.title: Direct connection
direct.description: Home Assistant will find Play devices on its own subnet automatically. If your speakers are on a different VLAN or subnet, list their IP addresses here (comma separated) — you can read them from the UniFi Network client list or the Play mobile app.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-enter your UniFi Play API key
reauth_confirm.description:
The console at {host} is no longer accepting the stored API key. This usually means the key was revoked or rotated, or the console was rebuilt. Create a new key under Settings → Control Plane → API Keys on that console and paste it whole.

To point Home Assistant at a different console, remove this entry and add a new one — a different console is a different set of speakers.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the console. Check the IP or hostname is correct and reachable from Home Assistant, and that you entered it without https://. Enable debug logging for this integration (Settings → Devices & services → UniFi Play → ⋮ → Enable debug logging) and retry to capture more information.
error.invalid_auth: The console rejected the API key (HTTP 401). The Apollo application is installed, so this is purely a credential problem — create a new key under Settings → Control Plane → API Keys on this console and paste it whole.
error.forbidden: The console refused the API key (HTTP 403). API keys are per-console, so check the key was created on the console you entered and has not been revoked.
error.apollo_unavailable: This console has no Apollo application, which is what serves the UniFi Play API. Apollo installs itself when a console discovers UniFi Play hardware, but only where the package has been released for that console's model — on some models it never arrives. Go back and choose Direct connection instead: it does not need the console at all.
error.unsupported_api: The Apollo application answered but has no device API at the expected path. Your Apollo version may be newer or older than this integration supports — please open an issue including your console firmware and Apollo version.
error.cloud_host: That address is Ubiquiti's cloud (ui.com), which serves the Site Manager API — a different API that does not proxy Apollo, so this integration cannot use it. Enter your console's own IP address or local hostname instead, with an API key created on that console (Settings → Control Plane → API Keys).
error.no_devices_found: No UniFi Play devices answered on Home Assistant's subnet. If your speakers are on a different VLAN or subnet, enter their IP addresses in the field above. Otherwise check they are powered on and reachable from Home Assistant.
error.no_response: The addresses you entered answered neither the discovery probe (UDP 10001) nor an MQTT connection (TCP 8883). Check each IP is correct and that no firewall rule blocks those ports between Home Assistant and the speakers.
error.discovery_failed: Could not open a discovery socket. Check the Home Assistant logs for details.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant logs for details.
error.console_busy: The console answered, but with a rate-limit or server error rather than data. That is usually temporary — a console mid-upgrade or under load. Wait a moment and try again.

abort.already_configured_device: Those speakers are already set up by "{entry}". A UniFi Play device can only belong to one entry: a second one covering the same hardware creates no entities at all, because every entity ID it would use is already taken. Remove the existing entry first if you want to set them up a different way.
abort.reauth_successful: The new API key was accepted and UniFi Play has reloaded.

play_announcement.name: Play announcement
play_announcement.description: Play a prerecorded announcement clip immediately. The clip must already be on the speaker — upload it in the UniFi Play app first. Whatever is streaming is paused for the duration.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The UniFi Play speaker to act on.

filename.name: File name
filename.description: Name of a clip already stored on the speaker. Read it from the Announcements sensor's files attribute rather than from the UniFi Play app — the app's label is not the filename (a clip shown as "17" is really "New Recording 17.m4a"), and a wrong name fails silently.

length.name: Length
length.description: Clip duration in seconds. Leave empty to use the duration the speaker reported for this clip.

zone_play.name: Play across zone
zone_play.description: Play on every speaker in the zone rather than just this one.

stop_announcement.name: Stop announcement
stop_announcement.description: Stop an announcement that is currently playing and resume whatever was interrupted.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The UniFi Play speaker to act on.

delete_announcement_file.name: Delete announcement clip
delete_announcement_file.description: Remove a prerecorded announcement clip from the speaker. Clips can only be added from the UniFi Play app.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The UniFi Play speaker to act on.

filename.name: File name
filename.description: Name of a clip already stored on the speaker. Read it from the Announcements sensor's files attribute rather than from the UniFi Play app — the app's label is not the filename (a clip shown as "17" is really "New Recording 17.m4a"), and a wrong name fails silently.

set_alarm.name: Create or update alarm
set_alarm.description: Create an alarm on the speaker, or update an existing one by passing its ID. Alarms are scheduled and fired by the speaker itself, so they work whether or not Home Assistant is running.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The UniFi Play speaker to act on.

alarm_id.name: Alarm ID
alarm_id.description: ID of an existing alarm to update. Leave empty to create a new one.

name.name: Name
name.description: Label shown for the alarm in the UniFi Play app.

sound.name: Sound
sound.description: Alarm sound. One of Lunar Chimes, Cosmic Bounce, Digital Ripple, Island Breeze or Jungle Rhythm.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long the alarm sounds, in minutes.

repeat.name: Repeat on
repeat.description: Weekdays the alarm repeats, 0 = Sunday through 6 = Saturday. Leave empty for a one-shot alarm.

delete_alarm.name: Delete alarm
delete_alarm.description: Delete an alarm from the speaker by its ID.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The UniFi Play speaker to act on.

alarm_id.name: Alarm ID
alarm_id.description: ID of the alarm to delete, as listed by the Alarms sensor.

set_quiet_hours.name: Create or update quiet hours
set_quiet_hours.description: Create a quiet-hours window on the speaker, or update an existing one by passing its ID. During the window the speaker limits or silences playback.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The UniFi Play speaker to act on.

quiet_id.name: Quiet hours ID
quiet_id.description: ID of an existing window to update. Leave empty to create a new one.

repeat.name: Repeat on
repeat.description: Weekdays the window applies, 0 = Sunday through 6 = Saturday. Leave empty to apply once.

wind_down.name: Wind down
wind_down.description: Minutes spent fading into the window rather than starting abruptly.

delete_quiet_hours.name: Delete quiet hours
delete_quiet_hours.description: Delete a quiet-hours window from the speaker by its ID.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The UniFi Play speaker to act on.

quiet_id.name: Quiet hours ID
quiet_id.description: ID of the window to delete, as listed by the Quiet Hours sensor.

save_eq_preset.name: Save EQ preset
save_eq_preset.description: Save the speaker's current 10-band equalizer settings as a named preset. The preset then appears in the EQ Preset selector.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The UniFi Play speaker to act on.

name.name: Preset name
name.description: Name to save the current EQ table under.

delete_eq_preset.name: Delete EQ preset
delete_eq_preset.description: Delete a saved custom EQ preset from the speaker.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The UniFi Play speaker to act on.

name.name: Preset name
name.description: Name of the preset to delete.

rename_eq_preset.name: Rename EQ preset
rename_eq_preset.description: Rename a saved custom EQ preset.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The UniFi Play speaker to act on.

create_zone.name: Create zone
create_zone.description: Group two or more UniFi Play devices into a multi-room zone. All devices play in sync. Any device's physical input can optionally be broadcast to the rest of the zone. Note: if the UniFi Play mobile app is open at the same time, its zone writes may overwrite changes made here, as both use the same MQTT channel.

name.name: Zone name
name.description: Display name for the new zone.

host_device_id.name: Zone host
host_device_id.description: The device that leads the zone. All members follow its audio source and volume. Its physical input can optionally be broadcast to all members.

member_device_ids.name: Member devices
member_device_ids.description: Additional devices that join the zone. Each device can only be in one zone at a time.

delete_zone.name: Delete zone
delete_zone.description: Delete a zone. All devices return to standalone mode.

add_zone_member.name: Add zone member
add_zone_member.description: Add a device to an existing zone. A device can only be in one zone at a time — it must be removed from its current zone before it can join another.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The UniFi Play device to add to the zone.

remove_zone_member.name: Remove zone member
remove_zone_member.description: Remove a device from a zone. If it is the device currently hosting the zone, another member takes over automatically. A zone needs at least 2 devices, so removing the second-to-last one is refused — delete the zone instead.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The UniFi Play device to remove from the zone.

name.name: New name
name.description: The new display name for the zone.

play_zone_announcement.name: Play zone announcement
play_zone_announcement.description: Play a prerecorded announcement clip across every device in a zone simultaneously. The clip must already be on the host device — upload it in the UniFi Play app first.

entity_id.name: Zone
entity_id.description: The zone entity to play the announcement on.

filename.name: File name
filename.description: Name of a clip already stored on the host speaker, as listed by the Announcements sensor.

length.name: Length
length.description: Clip duration in seconds. Leave empty to use the duration the speaker reported for this clip.

stop_zone_announcement.name: Stop zone announcement
stop_zone_announcement.description: Stop an announcement currently playing across a zone and resume whatever was interrupted on each device.

entity_id.name: Zone
entity_id.description: The zone entity to stop the announcement on.

set_zone_index.name: Set zone display order
set_zone_index.description: Change the display order of a zone. Lower numbers appear first in the UniFi Play app.

group_index.name: Display order
group_index.description: Order index (0 = first). Lower values appear earlier in the UniFi Play app zone list.

create_zone.title: Create Zone
create_zone.description:
Select the devices to group into a zone. All devices in a zone play in sync. You can broadcast any device's physical input to the rest of the zone using Set audio source after creating it.

Devices already in another zone are not shown.

select_zone.title: Select Zone
select_zone.description: Choose the zone you want to modify or delete.

menu_options.add_zone_member: Add a device to this zone
menu_options.remove_zone_member: Remove a device from this zone

add_zone_member.title: Add Zone Member
add_zone_member.description: Choose a device to add to **{zone_name}**. Devices already in any zone are not shown.

remove_zone_member.title: Remove Zone Member
remove_zone_member.description: Choose a device to remove from **{zone_name}**. A zone needs at least 2 devices.

set_zone_source.title: Set Audio Source
set_zone_source.description: Choose how **{zone_name}** plays audio. Streaming lets each device play its own source independently. Broadcast wired source sends one device's physical input to all other devices in the zone.

set_zone_wb_device.title: Choose Broadcast Wired Source
set_zone_wb_device.description:
Select which device in **{zone_name}** broadcasts its wired input to the rest of the zone, then pick the input to use.

An Audio Port can broadcast eARC, Line In, S/PDIF or USB; a PowerAmp can broadcast eARC or Line In.

reorder_zone.title: Change Zone Order
reorder_zone.description: Set the display order index for **{zone_name}**. Lower numbers appear first in the UniFi Play app.

delete_zone.title: Delete Zone
delete_zone.description: Delete **{zone_name}**? All devices will return to standalone mode.

set_zone_broadcasting.title: Stream Broadcasting
set_zone_broadcasting.description:
Choose which targets advertise themselves to streaming clients (AirPlay, Spotify Connect, Cast) for **{zone_name}**.

**Zone Only** - only the zone is available for streaming audio.
**Zone & Devices** - both the zone and individual devices are available.
**Off** - neither the zone nor individual devices are available.

abort.no_zones: No zones exist yet. Create one first.
abort.not_enough_devices: A zone needs at least 2 devices, and fewer than that are available. Devices already in a zone cannot join another one.
abort.no_available_devices: Every device is already in a zone. Remove one from its current zone before adding it here.

error.resolve_failed: Could not find that device in the coordinator. Make sure it is online.
error.no_mqtt: No MQTT connection to that device. Check that it is reachable.
error.already_member: That device is already a member of this zone.
error.not_a_member: That device is not a member of this zone.
error.device_in_other_zone: One or more selected devices are already in another zone. A device can only be in one zone at a time — remove it from its current zone first.
error.input_not_on_device: That input is not available on the device you selected. An Audio Port has eARC, Line In, S/PDIF and USB; a PowerAmp has eARC and Line In.
error.zone_needs_two_devices: A zone needs at least 2 devices. Delete the zone instead of removing this device.

mqtt_certificate_rejected.title: {name} is offline
mqtt_certificate_rejected.description:
Home Assistant cannot talk to **{name}** ({ip}) over MQTT. The speaker rejected every client certificate this integration ships.

Firmware 1.0.41 rotated the MQTT certificate authority, which previously left every entity unavailable with no device-level signal. This integration now tries each bundled generation on connect. If this repair is still open after a Home Assistant restart, the speaker is using a CA we do not have yet. Please open a GitHub issue with the speaker model and firmware version.
